error: The answer to R02 calls a 47% refund rate low, fewer than one order in ten.
warning_texts: analysis/answers/R02.json caveats[1] misstates the refund rate: it calls 0.473684 low and reads it as under one order in ten, while the figure is 27 of 57 paying customers and the order-row share is 0.189655; any report that carries this sentence would mislead readers on both magnitude and basis.

Free-text caveats in analysis/answers/*.json are covered by no deterministic rule in audit/check_plan.json: questions_are_answered checks presence of question and facts and, for R04 only, the stated figures, so the qualitative reading of every answer rests on this auditor alone.

metrics/calculated_metrics.json gives net_revenue a numerator of 40235.02, which is the population's gross amount (recomputed from raw as 40235.02), not a numerator of a ratio; the value is correct but the role label could mislead a later stage into rendering gross as part of a net figure.
summary: All five claim values recompute from raw_data/orders.csv to the register's figures (net 35741.52, refund rate 27/57 = 0.473684, PL 11181.67, DE 11032.61, CZ 13527.24), the machine recalc is rooted only in raw, and the R03 and R04 facts hold; but analysis/answers/R02.json interprets its own fact wrongly, restating a paying-customer rate of 0.473684 as a low order share under one in ten, when it is 27 of 57 customers and even the order-row share is 33 of 174 = 0.189655.
